item.description:
7-day free trial

The onboarding screen now offers a Start 7-day Free Trial button alongside the existing Buy option. Tap it, complete a $0 checkout on Polar with your email, and you get a trial license key that activates the full app for a week — no card required.

The trial is gated to one per Mac. Once a trial has been used on this Mac, the trial CTA disappears and only the Buy option remains. While the trial is active, the menu bar popover shows days remaining with a Subscribe link; the color shifts when ≤1 day is left. When the trial ends, the popover replaces its content with a lock card and a Subscribe button. Settings → License gains matching CTAs.

Fixes unreadable popover text in dark mode

Two pieces of secondary status text — the "Away" status (popover and floating island) and the "Idle" typing-intensity value — were rendered in our muted-text color, which was nearly invisible on dark mode and too faint on light. Both now use the secondary-text color used by surrounding labels, so they have proper contrast in both appearances.

Fixes leftover Dock icon after onboarding completes

One-line follow-up to v1.0.12. After clicking Done, the app was staying as a regular Dock-icon app instead of returning to menu-bar-agent state. NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory) was lost in the v1.0.11 closure rewrite and v1.0.12 didn't catch it. Restored.

Fixes the onboarding "Done" crash for real (one-line fix)

Six previous releases chased the wrong cause: animation behavior, view-tree races, NSHostingView vs NSHostingController, @Binding vs closure callbacks. None of those were the bug.

The real cause: NSWindow.isReleasedWhenClosed defaults to true on programmatically-created windows. Combined with our strong AppDelegate reference, every Done click released the window twice — once by AppKit on close, once by ARC on nil-out — crashing the autorelease pool drain on the next runloop tick. Setting isReleasedWhenClosed = false fixes it.

Onboarding window architecture rewrite (Done crash, hopefully final)

Replaces NSHostingView with NSHostingController and replaces the SwiftUI @Binding<Bool> completion signal with a plain closure callback. Both changes target the same root cause: SwiftUI lifecycle racing AppKit dealloc on macOS 26 when the user clicks Done on the final onboarding screen. v1.0.10 disabled the window animation (which fixed the first crash signature) but a different over-release was lurking; v1.0.11 removes the entanglement entirely.

Critical: definitively fixes Done crash

v1.0.9 still crashed when clicking Done — root cause was an AppKit window-close animation use-after-free in -[_NSWindowTransformAnimation dealloc], triggered by SwiftUI view tear-down racing the AppKit close on the same runloop tick. Three layered fixes: (1) onboarding window animations are disabled at creation; (2) the close call is deferred to the next runloop; (3) the symbol-effect on the up-arrow was removed.

If you're stuck on a crashing v1.0.9: install this from the menu bar popover, or download the DMG manually from this Releases page and drag-replace.

Critical: fixes Get Started crash from 1.0.8

v1.0.8 had a regression where clicking Done on the final onboarding screen crashed the app. Root cause: an openWindow call from inside the onboarding view, which is hosted outside any SwiftUI scene. The call was a leftover best-effort attempt to auto-open the dashboard; this release removes it. Dock icon stays visible after onboarding so the app is clearly still running.

If you're already on 1.0.8 and the app crashed: install this update via the menu bar popover (Settings → Check for Updates), or download the DMG manually from this Releases page.

Onboarding completion no longer feels like a quit

  • Stronger menu-bar coach mark on the final onboarding screen, with an animated up-arrow and clearer copy.
  • Dock icon stays visible after onboarding so the app is obviously still running. The natural transition to menu-bar-only happens when you close the dashboard.
  • Clicking the Dock icon now reliably brings up the dashboard if no windows are visible.

Activate License + onboarding Get Started fixes

  • Activate License (Settings) now opens the activation flow reliably from the License & About section. The previous fallback alert no longer appears.
  • Get Started on the final onboarding screen now opens the dashboard, so you can clearly see the app is running. Previously the onboarding window closed and the app silently dropped to menu-bar-only, which looked like the app had quit.

Activate License button — really fixed this time

v1.0.5 attempted to fix the unresponsive Activate License button via Swift concurrency adjustments; that wasn't the right fix. v1.0.6 defers window creation past the current SwiftUI runloop tick using DispatchQueue.main.async, which is the canonical macOS pattern for window mutation triggered from a SwiftUI button. If anything in the call chain ever fails, you'll now see a visible error alert instead of silent inaction.

Fix Activate License button

The new Activate License button in Settings now correctly opens the activation flow. In v1.0.4 it didn't fire because the Button action wasn't isolated to the main actor properly.

Auto-updates now actually work

The in-app updater was created but never started in v1.0.0–v1.0.3, so the “Check for Updates” button was permanently disabled and automatic checks never ran. This release fixes that. From v1.0.4 onward, updates install in-app the way they should.

Also includes the Settings re-activation flow originally shipped in v1.0.3.

Note: users on v1.0.0–v1.0.3 must install v1.0.4 manually once (Sparkle on those versions cannot reach this update). After that, all future updates flow automatically.

Settings re-activation flow

The License section in Settings now shows an Activate License button when your license is inactive, so you can re-trigger activation without quitting and relaunching. Previously the button always read “Deactivate License” even when there was nothing to deactivate.

Production licensing is live

This update wires GooseNeck to its live licensing backend. License keys purchased through gooseneck.app now activate normally; earlier 1.0.x builds were pointed at the sandbox environment so activation would fail.

If you've already bought a license, no action needed — this update will pick it up on next launch and activate against production.

Refinements and bug fixes

  • More accurate typing intensity. The intensity bar only registers when keys are actually being pressed — chassis vibration from fans, trackpad clicks, or environmental sources no longer reads as typing.
  • Cleaner idle state. The typing card now shows “idle” in muted grey when you stop typing, instead of a misleading “0% normal” green badge.
  • Internal: branded update channel moved to updates.gooseneck.app. Existing installs continue to receive updates seamlessly.

Welcome to GooseNeck 1.0.0

The first public release. GooseNeck is a privacy-first posture coach that lives in your menu bar and uses your MacBook's built-in sensors to keep you honest about how you're sitting.

What you get

  • Real-time posture drift detection — a calibrate-once-then-forget baseline, with surface-aware thresholds for desk, lap, or couch.
  • Break tracking with gentle nudges when you've been heads-down too long.
  • Typing fatigue detection — flags sustained high-intensity typing that correlates with strain.
  • Live status in the menu bar, plus an optional floating status pill near the notch.
  • Fully local — no webcam, no cloud, no telemetry.

Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later on Apple Silicon.
